name: Markwalder Grading Scale for Chronic Subdural Haematoma

version.label: Markwalder grading scale (1981), grades 0–4
version.detail: Clinical grade from level of consciousness and neurological deficit.

purpose: Grades the clinical condition of patients with chronic subdural haematoma.
intendedPopulation: Patients with chronic subdural haematoma, at presentation and follow-up.

options.label: Grade 1: Alert and oriented; mild symptoms
options.detail: Mild symptoms such as headache; absent or mild neurological signs such as reflex asymmetry.

options.label: Grade 2: Drowsy or disoriented
options.detail: Variable neurological deficit such as hemiparesis.

options.label: Grade 3: Stuporous
options.detail: Responds appropriately to painful stimuli; severe focal signs such as hemiplegia.

options.label: Grade 4: Comatose
options.detail: No motor response to painful stimuli; decerebrate or decorticate posturing.

resultStates.label: Grade 0: neurologically normal
resultStates.summary: No neurological symptoms or signs at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes clinical status only; it does not describe haematoma size or recurrence risk.

resultStates.label: Grade 1: alert and oriented
resultStates.summary: Mild symptoms such as headache; absent or mild neurological signs such as reflex asymmetry.

resultStates.label: Grade 2: drowsy or disoriented
resultStates.summary: Variable neurological deficit such as hemiparesis.

resultStates.label: Grade 3: stuporous
resultStates.summary: Responds appropriately to painful stimuli; severe focal signs such as hemiplegia.
resultStates.detail: Assess airway, neurological status and reversible causes according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade 4: comatose
resultStates.summary: No motor response to painful stimuli; decerebrate or decorticate posturing.
resultStates.detail: Assess airway, neurological status and reversible causes according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: A five-grade clinical description of patients with chronic subdural haematoma.
Commonly used to report clinical status before and after treatment in studies.

clinicalInsights.text: Record the GCS alongside the grade; the grade combines consciousness and focal deficit.
Depressed consciousness with severe deficit: assess according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

limitations.text: Broad grades combine consciousness and focal deficit, so different presentations can share a grade.

limitations: Not designed as a prognostic score.
Grade 1 mixes asymptomatic signs with mild symptoms.

confounders.effect: Lower consciousness independently of the haematoma.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Haematoma size, midline shift or recurrence risk.

guideSections.what: A five-grade (0–4) clinical scale for chronic subdural haematoma based on consciousness and neurological deficit.
guideSections.whenToUse: Documenting clinical status in chronic subdural haematoma, and reporting outcomes in studies.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess consciousness, orientation, symptoms and focal deficit, and choose the grade that fits.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Use with imaging, GCS and comorbidity; the grade alone does not decide management.

sources.citation: Markwalder TM, Steinsiepe KF, Rohner M, Reichenbach W, Markwalder H. The course of chronic subdural hematomas after burr-hole craniostomy and closed-system drainage. J Neurosurg. 1981;55(3):390-396.
Markwalder TM. Chronic subdural hematomas: a review. J Neurosurg. 1981;54(5):637-645.
